text:
Boston visits Dallas tonight with the numbers pointing to a close game. The model projects 2.68 expected goals for BOS and 2.83 for DAL (expected goals measure the quality of chances taken). At five on five, BOS has held 53% of the expected goals and DAL 49%, so there isn't much between them. DAL has the better power play (0.75 expected goals a game to 0.47) and the stingier penalty kill (0.50 allowed to 0.66). BOS also takes 4.78 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays.

Both projected goalies are hot. Jeremy Swayman (BOS) is at +6.63 goals saved above expected this season, meaning he has stopped that many more than an average goalie would have on the same shots. Jake Oettinger (DAL) is at +9.07, and last season he was at +2.15 to Swayman's +26.52. BOS has won five straight (5-0-0), but only 52% of the expected goals in those games backs it, and the Bruins' goal difference is running well ahead of their chances. DAL is 3-1-1 in its last five with 47% of the expected goals, so it has been getting results while being outplayed. Only Swayman's and Oettinger's recent runs are priced into the model.

David Pastrnak has a 28% chance to score and a 71% chance to record a point, riding a five-game point streak. Pavel Zacha could return from injury and is day-to-day. For DAL, Jason Robertson is the likeliest scorer at 36%, and Wyatt Johnston (34%) is due after six games without a goal on 2.7 expected goals.
